summary: SOFT-ARCHIVE + OWNERSHIP HARDENING VERIFIED (backend only). New file /app/backend/tests/test_e4_soft_archive_and_ownership.py — 32/32 tests PASS. Existing /app/backend/tests/test_e3_security_regression.py — 26/26 tests PASS (no E3 regression). Combined 58/58. All four evidentiary DELETE endpoints (extra-hours, reports, issues, elements) now soft-archive (status='zarchiwizowany') and never call delete_one/delete_many on their collections. Static grep on server.py confirms this: no db.daily_reports.delete_*, no db.extra_hours.delete_*, no db.issues.delete_*, no db.elements.delete_*. Only db.project_members.delete_many/delete_one remains (correct — junction table). PUT /api/reports/{id} now enforces author-or-admin/foreman ownership (previously any logged-in user could edit any report). Archived rows are correctly excluded from GET listings via q.setdefault('status', {'$ne': 'zarchiwizowany'}). extra_hours already-in-settlement returns 409 for both owner and admin. Seed admin@bzone.app NOT touched — post-run login still 200.
action_items: None — all requested fixes verified. Optional hardening: also apply the same author-or-admin/foreman ownership guard to PUT /issues (if exposed) and to any other update endpoints that currently rely only on current_user without owner check.
Optional cleanup: preview DB has accumulated ~30 test_* archived users from repeated regression runs; harmless but can be purged later.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1001-1013 delete_extra — correct order: 404 first, then perms (owner OR admin/foreman -> 403), then 409 on ujete_w_rozliczeniu_id, then update status='zarchiwizowany'. Audit as 'archiwizacja_godzin_ekstra'.

server.py:1171-1182 update_report — NEW ownership check: `r.get('user_id') != user['id'] and rola not in (admin,foreman) -> 403`. Closes the previous vulnerability where any logged-in user could PUT any report.
server.py:1214-1224 delete_report — same ownership pattern, soft archive only, audit 'archiwizacja_raportu'.
server.py:1304-1314 delete_issue — same pattern; author OR admin/foreman -> archive.

server.py:1812-1822 delete_element — UNIFIED archive: no status-based branching; every status (do_wykonania / zgloszony_gotowy / odebrany / itd.) archives via update_one. Verified in tests test_do_wykonania_archives / test_zgloszony_gotowy_archives / test_odebrany_archives.
server.py:972 / 1122 / 1260 — list endpoints all use q.setdefault('status', {'$ne': 'zarchiwizowany'}) so archived rows drop out of GET while remaining in DB for evidentiary/audit purposes.
grep verified: `db\.(daily_reports|extra_hours|issues|elements)\.(delete_one|delete_many)` returns ZERO matches in server.py. Only db.project_members.delete_* remains, which is correct.
Suggestion for future: consider archiving-via-projection helper (single `_archive(collection, id, user)` function) — currently the pattern is repeated 4 times; low priority.

rca_of_issue: FIX VERIFICATION: The historical incident (hard-deleted user account) prompted a broader audit that revealed 4 additional endpoints performing db.<col>.delete_one on evidentiary data (billing hours, daily reports, quality issues, plan elements) and one endpoint (PUT /reports/{id}) missing an ownership check. All five have been fixed: (a) DELETE endpoints now `update_one({'$set': {'status': 'zarchiwizowany'}})` + audit; (b) permission gates enforce author-or-admin/foreman with 403 for other users; (c) 409 conflict preserved on extra_hours with ujete_w_rozliczeniu_id; (d) elements archive UNIFORMLY across all status values (no more delete_one on 'zgloszony_gotowy' or 'do_wykonania'). GET listing queries hide archived rows via q.setdefault so the UX is unchanged while the underlying rows remain immutable evidence. A static grep test in the suite prevents accidental re-introduction of hard-delete on these four collections.
